sentence: Start with a rope that hugs the planet, about forty thousand kilometers long.
claim: The rope round the equator is about 40,000 km: pi x 12,756 km = 40,074 km.
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. The page gives the diameter, not the length: the circumference is computed (pi x diameter). Equator 40,075 km is the standard figure.
builder_read: "With an equatorial diameter of 7,926 miles (12,756 kilometers), Earth is the biggest of the terrestrial planets"

sentence: But a circle's length is two times pi times its radius, the distance to its center.
claim: Circumference = 2 x pi x radius (a mathematical definition).
source_title: Derivation (calc.py): geometry of a circle, 2 x pi x r; no outside page
note: DERIVATION: the length of a circle is 2 x pi x its radius (a definition). Not taken from any page. OPEN until a person re-does the sum.

sentence: Lift the rope a meter, and the radius grows a meter.
claim: Lifting the rope evenly by 1 m raises the circle's radius by 1 m (idealised: a perfect sphere, a smooth rope).
source_title: Derivation (calc.py): geometry of a circle, 2 x pi x r; no outside page
note: DERIVATION: the thought experiment's assumption, badged on screen: a perfect sphere, a smooth rope, no sag. Lifting by 1 m adds 1 m to the radius. Not taken from any page.

sentence: So the rope grows by two times pi times one meter, a bit over six meters.
claim: New length minus old length = 2 pi (R + 1 m) - 2 pi R = 2 pi x 1 m = 6.28 m: R cancels. calc.py: extra_m = 6.3 for the Earth, a ball and the Sun.
source_title: Derivation (calc.py): geometry of a circle, 2 x pi x r; no outside page
note: DERIVATION: 2 x pi x 1 m = 6.28 m. Checkable by hand with a hula hoop. Not taken from any page.

sentence: That is about four of you, lying head to toe.
claim: 6.28 m / 1.7 m (an adult's height, assumption) = 3.7: 'about four of you'.
source_title: Assumption: an adult is about 1.7 m tall; arithmetic 2π × 1 m ÷ 1.7 m = 3.7
note: ASSUMPTION (no source page): a person about 1.7 m tall. The division is arithmetic. Shown in the film as the badge "∵ 1.7 m a person".

sentence: Try a basketball or the Sun: lift the rope one meter, and the extra rope is the same.
claim: The extra rope is the same 6.3 m for a basketball (radius about 12 cm), the Earth (6,378 km) and the Sun (diameter about 1.4 million km).
source_title: Derivation (calc.py): geometry of a circle, 2 x pi x r; no outside page
note: DERIVATION (calc.py: sens_m): 2 x pi x 1 m is the same for any radius (a basketball, the Earth, the Sun). Inputs: the radii of the three bodies; the Earth and Sun sizes are claim c9 and c1. Not taken from any page.

sentence: The planet's size cancels out: only the lift matters.
claim: extra = 2 pi h: the planet's radius is not in the answer.
source_title: Derivation (calc.py): geometry of a circle, 2 x pi x r; no outside page
note: DERIVATION: follows from c2 and c4; the radius cancels. Not taken from any page.

sentence: Ten times higher needs ten times more rope.
claim: extra = 2 pi h is proportional to h: 10 m gives 63 m (shown on screen).
source_title: Derivation (calc.py): geometry of a circle, 2 x pi x r; no outside page
note: DERIVATION: follows from c4: 2 x pi x 10 m = 62.8 m. Not taken from any page.
